DR-12.question: Keep the boring-spacing question as a dedicated build, or make it ordinary suite tasks once you supply real investigation plans?
DR-12.why: It was the driving example of the 2026-09-13 reset, but no agent can reach the spacing maths, and it cannot be measured without real plans. Today the question risks a plausible wrong number rather than a refusal.
DR-12.background: planlens/ir/spatial.py computes spacing three ways: nearest neighbour; density-equivalent sqrt(area/n), which is what 'borings at 50-ft centres' means; and the mean of all pairs. It reports the spread between them: on a regular 3x3 grid they differ by 2.45x, so the API deliberately has no single 'average spacing'. The `measure` tool now reads distances off drawings, but nothing on the review page calls spatial.py. Blocked on OWN-38: the original driving sheet is in neither repo, and 2-4 more subsurface-investigation plans are needed as ground truth. The approved plan file it cites is also missing (DOC-15).

options.label: Suite tasks, all three conventions reported
options.effect: You supply 3-5 plans; an agent adds tasks whose checks expect each convention with its definition and the spread. General capability, no question-specific prompt rule.

options.label: Dedicated vertical slice, as first planned
options.effect: Wire spatial.py into the review page as its own path, tuned on this question. Quicker to demonstrate; risks fitting one example.

options.label: Drop it
options.effect: Close DR-12; spatial.py stays in planlens unused. Spacing questions are answered, if at all, by the general measuring tools.

DR-12.recommendation: Suite tasks. Supply the plans (OWN-38); report all three conventions with their definitions, per your 'methods open to assumptions' rule, and let the suite judge rather than tuning prompts to this one question.
DR-12.if_no_answer: Stays Later and blocked on OWN-38; nothing is built.
